title: Regulatory incident assertion and audit evidence guide
body:
Purpose
This draft is a customer-facing communications + evidence guide specifically designed for enterprise and regulated customers who require audit-ready assertions after an inference service incident. It pairs short status updates suitable for a public status page with a parallel technical appendix and an evidence package checklist that satisfies compliance reviewers.

Usage guidance (who should send what)
- Customer Success lead (owner): high-level status page wording, enrollment invitation for evidence package.
- Engineering SRE: technical appendix, timeline, and signed hash of logs.
- Security/Compliance: statement on data access, retention, and any regulatory obligations.
- Account executive or customer legal contact: coordinate sharing method and NDA checks.

1) Recommended public status page entry (short)
- Title: Partial degradation of inference responses in eu-west-1 (resolved)
- Impact: From 2026-07-04 03:10 UTC to 2026-07-04 04:20 UTC some requests returned delayed or truncated responses for a subset of customers in eu-west-1.
- Current status: Resolved — normal service restored 2026-07-04 04:20 UTC.
- Next steps: We are compiling a customer-specific evidence package for regulated customers who request it; contact cs-alerts@redwood.ai to request.

2) Technical short form (on status page, slightly expanded)
- Root cause (short): Autoscaling bug in the inference router allowed stale KV cache references to persist during a scale-down, causing incomplete token streaming for affected shards.
- Mitigation: We deployed a conservative scale policy and an immediate cache invalidation script; we also added a short-term rate limiter for shard reattach events.

3) Enterprise postmortem summary for customers (one page)
- Incident window: 2026-07-04 03:10 — 04:20 UTC
- Affected surface: approx. 2.3% of requests routed to eu-west-1 serving pool; mostly long-sequence streaming sessions (>=1024 tokens) and a small set of tenants pinned to older model variants.
- User-visible symptoms: delayed streaming, truncated responses, occasional 502 after partial tokens were emitted. No data loss reported.
- Immediate remediation: cache invalidation, rollback of scale policy, targeted restart of 11 serving nodes.
- Current mitigations in place: conservative autoscale thresholds, additional health checks during scale-down, temporary pin migration help for affected tenants.

4) Audit-ready assertions (language for legal/compliance teams)
- Data integrity assertion: We have verified via retained request/response logs and checksums that no user payloads were altered. Original request bodies and final responses are intact for all persisted records in the evidence package.
- Data exposure assertion: No unauthorized access to customer data was detected. Only platform services with standard operator privileges performed actions; access logs are included in the evidence package.
- Service continuity assertion: While some requests returned degraded outputs, there were no successful attempts to exfiltrate or modify customer data.
- Root cause assertion: The regression that allowed stale KV cache references to persist was introduced in commit a1f3b2c during a scale policy change; this commit bypassed a previously-required cache flush on node detach.

5) Evidence package contents (what to include when a regulated customer requests the audit bundle)
- Executive summary (PDF): one-page incident summary, impact, mitigations, and follow-up schedule.
- Signed timeline (CSV + PGP-signed digest): minute-level timeline of operator and system events for the incident window and 30 minutes pre/post.
- Retained logs: anonymized request/response traces for affected tenant IDs (or full traces if requested under NDA), server logs, autoscaling events, and router traces.
- Checksums and hashes: Merkle-style digest file and per-log SHA256 hashes with signer identity from SRE lead.
- Config diffs: git diffs showing the scale policy change (commit id referenced) and rollback commit.
- Mitigation artifacts: cache invalidation script version, canary config used for rollback, and health-check outputs.
- Forensics notes: list of investigators, times of access, limits of evidence collection, and any gaps.
- Contact and approval: named compliance contact, signed cover letter (PDF) from Redwood legal (if requested).

6) Delivery options and controls (customer choices)
- Public bundle: executive summary + non-sensitive timeline + redacted logs (no customer payloads).
- NDA-protected bundle: full logs and traces shared via secure transfer after NDA in place.
- On-site review: coordinate with Security to mediate a virtual walkthrough for auditors.
- Retention window: evidence stored for 90 days by default; for audit requests we can extend retention for up to 1 year under contract amendment.

7) Suggested email/Slack template to invite customer to request evidence
Subject: Evidence package available for recent eu-west-1 incident (2026-07-04)
Hi <Customer Security Contact>,
We’ve published a status update about the transient inference degradation in eu-west-1 on 2026-07-04. If your compliance team requires an audit-ready evidence package (signed timeline, logs, checksums), reply to this message or request via the support portal and we’ll initiate secure transfer. Please indicate whether you need a redacted bundle or full traces under NDA.
Regards,
Aisha (on behalf of Customer Success)

8) Customer verification snippets (short technical checks customers can run quickly)
- Verify request timestamps: compare your SDK client timestamps to the signed timeline to confirm observed latency windows.
- Response integrity: request a small sample of persisted responses from our evidence package and validate SHA256(payload) matches local copy.
- Model pin fingerprint: confirm model hash for pinned variants in your config matches the model hash included in the evidence bundle.

9) Follow-up roadmap and commitments (what we will do next)
- Short term (0–2 weeks): backport explicit cache-flush on node detach, add unit/integration tests for scale-down, expand canary coverage to longer-sequence requests.
- Medium term (2–8 weeks): automated proof-of-integrity pipeline for incident timelines (PGP-signed artifacts), per-tenant re-run tool for affected requests, optional extended retention for enterprise bundles.
- Long term (quarter): policy and runtime changes to avoid stale KV handles, UI visibility for pin migrations, and a dedicated audit-officer runbook.

10) FAQ for compliance reviewers
Q: Were customer secrets exposed?
A: No. Access was limited to platform operator accounts and automated services; no external IPs accessed customer payloads. Access logs are included in the evidence package.
Q: Can you prove immutability of logs?
A: We provide per-file SHA256 hashes and a signed digest of the evidence bundle. We are working toward a Merkle-tree based proof in Q3.
Q: How do you handle requests for extended retention?
A: Extended retention for audit artifacts is available under contract; contact your account executive for amendment.

11) Internal checklist before release to customer
- [ ] Legal sign-off on any non-redacted logs
- [ ] Security review of artifacts to avoid PII leakage beyond contract scope
- [ ] SRE signs and timestamps the event timeline
- [ ] Customer Success drafts the outreach message and service credit options if applicable
- [ ] Compliance confirms retention window for shared artifacts

Appendix: engineer-facing timeline extract (example lines)
2026-07-04T03:09:47Z router: scale-down initiated pool eu-west-1 (change request id: cr-9812)
2026-07-04T03:10:12Z node-84: flush-cache skipped due to race condition in detach handler (commit a1f3b2c)
2026-07-04T03:12:05Z alerts: increased 502-rate on router (service=false positives on partial streams)
2026-07-04T03:35:40Z SRE: launched cache-invalidation rollout (script v1.2)
2026-07-04T04:20:02Z service: router metrics returned to baseline; 0.3% error-rate sustained

Notes / open questions for internal review
- Need to confirm whether tenants pinned to older model variants should be proactively migrated or offered assisted migration.
- Decide retention SLA for audit artifacts (default 90 days vs 1 year for enterprise).

This document is intended to be customer-facing when combined with the produced evidence package and legal sign-off. Use conservative redaction for any PII or customer-only artifacts unless an NDA is in place.
